what: Criterion 5: one substitution per half of the change, each run against the committed state of the half it attacks, each showing which check goes red. Rule 9 of docs/engineering/DEVELOPMENT_PACE.md.

state.why: Both mutants are applied to the committed fix and reverted with git checkout afterwards, not to the working copy before the commit: a mutant reverted over an uncommitted change takes the change with it (measured on Issue #147).

greenBaseline.output: Пройден!: не пройдено 0, пройдено 25, пропущено 0, всего 25

mutant1.half: The first pass: every label bids exactly its name.
mutant1.was:
private static int FirstAttempt(WorldLabelRequest request) =>
        Math.Min(1, request.Lines.Count);
mutant1.became:
private static int FirstAttempt(WorldLabelRequest request) =>
        request.Rank is WorldLabelRank.Hovered or WorldLabelRank.Selected
            ? request.Lines.Count
            : Math.Min(1, request.Lines.Count);
mutant1.meaning: The exemption Issue #371 introduced, put back: a focused label lays its whole text in the first pass again.

criterion1.verbatim: Assert.Equal() Failure: Collections differ / Expected: ["Raider#17", "Raider#18", "Raider#20"] / Actual: ["Raider#17", "Raider#20"]
criterion1.reading: Raider#18 is «Долговязый», and he is missing from the frame the game would draw while «Сиплый» is focused — the defect of Issue #379 verbatim.

alsoRed: WorldLabelFocusTests.The_line_the_crowd_took_off_a_caption_comes_back_under_the_pointer_where_there_is_room — «Сиплый» is laid with two lines again on the crowded cell, which is the same purchase seen from the other side.

WorldLabelFocusTests.The_body_under_the_cursor_is_offered_its_sentence_first — the constructed frame loses a label (4 expected, 3 placed), because a two-line bid in the first pass takes a place a name was going to use.

mutant2.half: The second pass: the focused label is offered its sentence first.
mutant2.meaning: The focus keeps its place in the first pass and loses its priority in the second: the sentences are offered back in scene order, so a neighbour standing earlier in the scene takes the one place that fits.

criterion4.verbatim: Assert.Equal() Failure: Values differ / Expected: 2 / Actual: 1
criterion4.reading: The body under the cursor is laid with one line of its two: «Косой», who stands earlier in scene order, grew into the only place a sentence fits. Nothing else in the two files goes red, which is the point — the two halves are separately load-bearing.

whatTheMutantsDoNotClaim: Mutant 2 changes no frame of today's owner scene, and that is stated rather than hidden: the second pass already walked the list in rank order because the first pass built it that way. GrowingOrder makes that promise a statement of the code instead of a side effect of a sort ten lines above it, and the constructed scene of the check is what can tell the two apart.
